newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor mulls cutting production.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor mulls cutting production.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest carmaker, is considering cutting production because of rising inventory, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
"We are studying various measures to reduce inventories," the spokesman said. "We are considering cutting production by not allowing overtime work for a while. But nothing has been decided yet."
South Korean carmakers normally operate assembly lines for 20 hours a day, which includes four hours of overtime work.
He said inventories in Hyundai Motor totalled about 50,000 vehicles at end-March. No compatative figures were given.
The Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association, citing a slump in local car sales, urged the government to ease restrictions.
"We asked the government to revise rules and the tax system, which depress vehicle demand," said an association spokemsan.
Another association official said vehicle inventories hit a high last month, far outpacing the previous record of 100,000 units. Bit he declined to give the exact figure.
Kia Motors Corp and Daewoo Motor Co, an unlisted affiliate of the Daewoo Group, said they had no immediate plan to reduce working hours.
